text:
Maya (Support): Customer reporting repeated 413s when sending large embedding uploads via our HTTP client. They say they batch ~1,200 items of 1,024-dim vectors in one request. Account: acct_9Z3L. They tried gzip + chunked transfer; still fails. Can we triage? :frowning:

Tom (Eng-API): 413 = request entity too large. First check: what front proxy is hitting the limit (NGINX/LB)? Also the model dim mismatch error sometimes shows up if vectors in the same payload have different lengths. Do we have the raw request headers or x-request-id?

Maya (Support): Customer pasted response headers: HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large, x-request-id: r-9a12f, and their client logs show Content-Length: 18,512,000 for the failing attempt. They say 1,200 vectors * 1024 dims * decimal ascii is huge.

Ivan (Infra): Quick rules: nginx client_max_body_size operates on post-decompressed body by default. Gzip won't help unless the whole stack checks compressed size (rare). For hosted tenants default is 10m on public edge. Dedicated tenants often have a higher or configurable limit.

Ruth (DevEx): For embedding payload sizing, binary float32 per component is 4 bytes, but JSON text floats are many bytes. For 1024 dims, an average text encoding can be ~6-10 bytes per dim. Rough: 1024 * 7 ~ 7KB per vector. So 1,200 vectors -> ~8.4MB just for numbers plus JSON overhead -> crosses 10MB easily, consistent with 18MB Content-Length customer reported (maybe string formatting).

Tom (Eng-API): Immediate customer guidance: chunk client dataset into smaller batches. We suggest aiming for <8-10 MB uncompressed bodies. For 1024-dim vects that might mean 200-800 vectors per request depending on float formatting. Also confirm they aren't sending redundant metadata per vector.

customer-app: Is there any streaming / resumable embeddings upload? We have flaky network and want to resume partial uploads.

Ruth (DevEx): Not yet public. Short-term workaround: client-side resumable uploads by numbering chunks and persisting progress. Example pattern: upload 200 vectors at a time, on success mark chunk id done, on failure retry. We'll share a sample client snippet. Long-term: we have a product request to add multipart/resumable import for embeddings.

Maya (Support): They also reported intermittent "dimension mismatch (expected 1024 got 512)" after retries. Could be some rows generated by an older encoder in the pipeline. I asked them to validate shapes before sending.

Tom (Eng-API): Dimension mismatch is server-side validation. Recommend they run a quick local validator. Example snippet I usually send:
```python
def check_shapes(batch, expected=1024):
    bad = [(i,len(v)) for i,v in enumerate(batch) if len(v) != expected]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f\"bad shapes: {bad[:5]}\")
```
Also ask them to print min/max len and sample rows.

Ivan (Infra): From our access logs we saw a cluster of failed uploads with x-request-ids r-9a12f and r-9a15c. The ingress returned nginx 413 before the request reached app nodes. So it's ingress limit. If acct_9Z3L is Dedicated we can bump their ingress limit temporarily; if Hosted it's trickier. I'll check tenancy.

Maya (Support): Customer provided sanitized body example (first 3 vectors). They are serialized as arrays of floats, no compression on individual numbers. They tried chunked transfer-encoding but still got 413.

Ivan (Infra): Chunked transfer-encoding doesn't bypass client_max_body_size in most setups because nginx still reads and enforces limits. Also, if client sends Content-Length but body ends up larger, you'll get mismatches and errors. Make sure they don't set an incorrect Content-Length when streaming.

customer-app: They also noticed a 400 sometimes with message "request body incomplete" when they used a streaming generator in their Python client.

Tom (Eng-API): That points to mismatched Content-Length or broken chunking. For Python requests, if you pass a generator, requests will stream without a content-length unless you set it yourself. If middleware mutates the payload bytes (like encoding changes), that can cause mismatch. Suggest they use simple POST with a bytes payload for tests.

Maya (Support): I asked them to run a small battery of tests and return the failing x-request-ids. Proposed test plan:
- sanity: send 1-5 vectors (text) to confirm API key and model selection
- incremental batches: 100, 300, 600, 900, 1200 vectors using identical formatting and record Content-Length and x-request-id
- send the sanitized first/failing payload and Content-Length header when 413 occurs
- include a single-run shape validator output

Ruth (DevEx): I'll draft a helper script for them to reproducibly chunk and upload with concurrency and retry. Example snippet we made lighter for the customer:
```python
import requests

def send_chunks(vectors, chunk=300):
    for i in range(0, len(vectors), chunk):
        payload = {"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":vectors[i:i+chunk]}
        r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json=payload, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer ...'})
        print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
```
This helps find the threshold and keeps requests idempotent per chunk.

customer-app: Ran tests. Results: 100 OK (x-request-id r-9a20a, CL 1,650,432), 300 OK (r-9a21b, CL 4,980,120), 600 -> 413 (r-9a12f, CL 10,120,003), 900 -> 413 (r-9a15c, CL 15,300,250). Attached the x-request-ids.

Ivan (Infra): Confirmed acct_9Z3L is on Hosted edge (shared pool), not Dedicated. Per-tenant increase is possible but requires product approval due to DoS risk. For now advise chunking <=300 for their current encoder style. I'll file INF-4892 to evaluate raising host pool to 30m for specific clients with rate limits.

Tom (Eng-API): Regarding dimension mismatch: analyze the failing payloads they sent. Found sparse pattern: ~0.8% of vectors in batches were 512-dim. Likely from a mixed pipeline that sometimes calls a different encoder or truncates errors. Recommend they dedupe and check pipeline hooks that produce embeddings.

Maya (Support): I asked customer to add pre-send validation and to re-run their pipeline to fix generator drift. They implemented chunking (300 per request) and retried full upload; progress succeeded with 0 failures after retries. They still asked for a resumable feature; logged as FR-2219.

Ruth (DevEx): I'll publish a short support post in #support-templates on recommended chunk sizes per model dimension and examples for Python/Go. Will include notes: - gzip won't avoid nginx body limit; - chunked transfer encoding doesn't bypass checks; - ensure Content-Length accurate or omitted when streaming; - prefer small atomic chunks + client-side resume.

Ivan (Infra): For telemetry: added logs to correlate Content-Length, actual body bytes, and client IP for 413s to help customers debug. Also flagged anomalous requests where declared CL < actual bytes.

Tom (Eng-API): Closing loop: customer fixed pipeline, used 300-vector chunks, retried and completed job. They may request a hosted limit increase later; we'll handle per-account. Thanks all. :tada:

Maya (Support): Marking resolved. Will attach guidance doc and the DevEx snippet.

-- end of thread --
